chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Al-Marzuban ibn Imran said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'I intend to travel, so should I fast for the month in which I travel?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'. I said, 'So when I return, do I make it up?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, just as you did not fast, similarly you do not make it up.'

key_terms.الشَّهْر: The month (specifically Ramadan in this context)

ai.seo_question: Do I need to make up Ramadan fasts if I travel during the month?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) establishes a unique ruling where the missed fasts are not merely deferred but are entirely excused, likening the non-fast to the non-payment of a debt. This interpretation, found in *Al-Kafi*, highlights the severity of the hardship of travel, suggesting that the obligation is lifted rather than postponed, distinguishing it from the standard practice of *qada* (making up) fasts after Ramadan.
